title: PRAHAAR
body_text:
The Ministry of Home Affairs has unveiled ‘PRAHAAR’ as India's first comprehensive National Counter Terrorism Policy & Strategy on 23 rd February, 2026. It provides a national counter-terrorism framework for prevention  of,  and responding   to  terrorist  activities  and  radicalization
through coordinated "whole of government" and “whole of society” approaches. ‘PRAHAAR’ strategy & policy is predicated on the following pillars:
Prevention of terror attacks to protect Indian citizens and interests; Responses, which are swift and proportionate to the threat posed;
iii. Aggregating internal capacities for achieving synergy in a whole-of-government approach; iv. Human rights and ‘Rule of Law’ based processes for mitigation of threats;
Attenuating the conditions conducive to terrorism, including radicalization;
vi. Aligning and shaping the international efforts to counter terrorism;
Recovery and resilience through a whole-of-society approach.
‘PRAHAAR’ addresses all counter-terrorism objectives through a comprehensive, intelligence-led proactive framework built upon a seven-pillar strategy. It shifts India from a reactive security stance to a proactive doctrine by formalizing real-time intelligence sharing through the Multi Agency Centre (MAC), securing critical infrastructure, and deploying a swift, coordinated chain of command between State agencies/Police and Specialized Central Forces like the National Security Guard (NSG). Simultaneously, it integrates cutting-edge technology, strictly upholds the
Rule of Law and human rights, and implements community-collaborative counter-radicalization modules to dismantle the terror ecosystem.
It also counters terror financing by tracing crypto wallets, choking dark web crowdsourcing, and seizing assets through Central Agencies. It aligns with Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards and uses international treaties to block cross-border state-sponsored terror funding networks.
The Government of India is committed to the progressive and phased implementation of the 'PRAHAAR' strategy. This approach prioritizes immediate institutional and systems integration while thoroughly assessing performance outcomes through a framework of layered oversight mechanisms.
In addition to the regular monitoring and assessments, one such mechanism is organizing Annual ‘Anti-Terror Conference (ATC)’ by the NIA under the aegis of the Ministry of Home Affairs, which serves as an important platform to review and strengthen its counter-terrorism strategy by bringing together senior officials from law enforcement agencies, intelligence organizations, security forces, policymakers, and legal experts.
The Anti-Terror Conference enables stakeholders to assess the effectiveness of existing counterterrorism measures, identify operational/
administrative gaps and preparedness, recommend policy, legal & institutional reforms, and promote collaboration, capacity building, and a coordinated national response to strengthen and continuously evolve India's counterterrorism framework in response to an increasingly dynamic security environment.
This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha that it launched 'PRAHAAR', India's first comprehensive National Counter Terrorism Policy & Strategy, on 23 February 2026. Built on seven pillars, it adopts a 'whole of government' and 'whole of society' approach covering prevention, proportionate response, capacity aggregation, rule-of-law compliance, counter-radicalization, international alignment, and resilience. It strengthens real-time intelligence sharing via the Multi Agency Centre (MAC), coordinates State police with central forces like the NSG, targets terror financing including crypto wallets and dark web activity, and aligns with FATF standards. The NIA also organizes an Annual Anti-Terror Conference (ATC) to review and refine the strategy.
enrichment.context:
India's counter-terrorism architecture has historically evolved reactively, often shaped by responses to major attacks such as 26/11 Mumbai, which led to the creation of bodies like the NSG hubs, NATGRID, and the Multi Agency Centre (MAC) for intelligence sharing. PRAHAAR marks a shift toward a codified, proactive national doctrine that consolidates fragmented mechanisms into a unified strategy, addressing gaps in coordination among central agencies (NIA, IB, RAW) and state police forces. The emphasis on 'whole of society' engagement reflects lessons from global counter-radicalization models, recognizing that community-level de-radicalization and resilience-building are as crucial as kinetic responses.

The strategy's focus on terror financing—tracing cryptocurrency wallets, disrupting dark web crowdfunding, and aligning with FATF standards—reflects growing global concern over technology-enabled terror funding, especially as FATF has previously scrutinized India's compliance and neighboring Pakistan's grey/black-listing status. The mention of blocking 'cross-border state-sponsored terror funding networks' implicitly references concerns about Pakistan-based terror financing. The institutionalization of an Annual Anti-Terror Conference by the NIA also formalizes a recurring review mechanism, akin to periodic strategic reviews used in other national security domains, ensuring the policy remains adaptive to evolving threats like lone-wolf radicalization, cyber-enabled terrorism, and hybrid warfare.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism through which PRAHAAR formalizes real-time intelligence sharing among agencies?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifies that PRAHAAR formalizes real-time intelligence sharing through the Multi Agency Centre (MAC).

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of India's National Counter Terrorism Policy & Strategy 'PRAHAAR' in shifting India's security posture from reactive to proactive. Examine its seven-pillar framework and its implications for internal security governance.

Terror financing through emerging technologies such as cryptocurrency and the dark web poses new challenges to national security. Critically evaluate the measures outlined in India's counter-terrorism strategy to address this threat, and assess India's alignment with international frameworks like the FATF.
